Apply cross-league EPV offsets to an EPR table (end-add, PSR-consistent)

Source: R/player_ratings_epv.R
apply_epr_league_offsets.Rd

Adds the per-league network offset to each row's epr_offensive / epr_defensive (and recomputes epr = epr_offensive + epr_defensive), placing league-season-centred EPR on a single Big-5-equivalent scale. This is the EPR analogue of apply_psr_league_offsets: run calculate_epr_regression with the league-season FE kept and league_offsets = NULL (so \(\beta_{player}\) is "above league-season mean"), then add the offset HERE.

Usage

apply_epr_league_offsets(epr_dt, offsets, verbose = FALSE)

Arguments

epr_dt

A data.table/data.frame with a league column and epr_offensive/epr_defensive (and optionally epr).

offsets

Offset table with columns league, offset_off, offset_def (e.g. from build_league_network() on offensive and defensive EPV).

verbose

Report how many rows were adjusted. Default FALSE.

Value

epr_dt (as data.table) with epr_offensive/ epr_defensive/epr shifted, plus an epr_league_offset column recording the applied total. Rows whose league has no offset are unchanged (offset 0).

Details

Why end-add rather than shifting \(y\) inside the regression: the offset is a league-LEVEL quantity (estimated from the whole co-occurrence network), so it should be applied at full strength, not discounted by each player's ridge shrinkage. Shifting \(y\) and shrinking \(\beta\) toward 0 pulls low-sample weak-league players back toward the GLOBAL mean — the opposite of the intent. Keeping the FE then end-adding shrinks each player toward their own LEAGUE prior, which is the correct behaviour (and matches PSR + unlocks the additive fast-path for offset-only changes).

See also

apply_psr_league_offsets, build_league_network

Other league offsets: apply_psr_league_offsets(), build_league_network(), compute_psr_league_offsets()
